action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The current board state shows the game in its early stages, with X at row 5, column 3, and O at row 4, column 3. O's move to stack on X in the center column prevents X from easily building a vertical line there using the bottom piece, but the bottom X remains useful for horizontal and diagonal connections. 

O has potential to build a vertical line upward from its piece at row 4, column 3, as there are enough rows above to reach 4 in a row if uninterrupted. However, immediately blocking by playing in column 3 is not necessary and wastes a move, as it doesn't create immediate threats for X and allows O freedom to build elsewhere.

Instead, the optimal strategy is to build a connected horizontal base at the bottom using the existing X in column 3, forcing O to defend and preventing O from safely developing the vertical threat in column 3. Playing in column 2 or 4 achieves this by placing an X adjacent to the existing one at row 5.

If O then ignores the horizontal build and plays in column 3 to start its vertical, X can follow by playing in the next adjacent column to create three in a row with open ends on both sides, creating two simultaneous threats that O cannot block in one move, leading to an immediate forced win for X.

Since O will play optimally and defend the horizontal build (e.g., by playing in column 0, 1, 5, or 6 to block an end or split the line), the game continues, but X has dictated the play, gained positional advantage with connected pieces, and can block the center vertical later if needed.

Columns 2 and 4 are symmetrically optimal. Selecting the smaller index.

Final Answer: 2

The current board shows X with two adjacent pieces on the bottom row in columns 2 and 3, with O pieces directly above them in row 4. No immediate win or threat exists for either player. Placing an X in column 4 drops to the bottom, creating three connected X's horizontally in columns 2-4 on row 5. This sets up two separate winning threats for X's next turn: placing in column 1 (for four in columns 1-4) or column 5 (for four in columns 2-5). O can block only one threat per turn and has no counter-threat that forces X to respond instead, ensuring X wins next. This is optimal over other moves, which do not force a win as immediately.
